nfl.injuries: midweek: practice reports plus ESPN's latest injury news for 28 of 28 teams; final statuses come with Friday's report (Saturday morning in Melbourne)
nfl.early_text: Player ratings still lean on last season for the first few weeks, so treat big disagreements with the bookies with extra care.
nfl.subtitle: Win chances and minimum prices from player ratings, unit matchups, injuries, rest, travel and weather, blended with the current betting price (60% stats this week). The stats-only pick is shown on every game.
nfl.foot_note: Win % = the stats model blended with the current moneyline (DraftKings via ESPN, else the nflverse listed line): 60% stats in weeks 1-9, where the stats beat the market in backtests, 0% from week 10, where the market knows more (rested starters, late injury news), and 30% in the playoffs. In the walk-forward backtest this beat the log loss of the closing line; the stats model alone did not. The reasons, injuries and "stats only" line on each game are the stats model by itself. Lines and totals here use NFL key numbers: margins of 3, 7, 10 and 14 and totals like 37, 41, 44 and 51 come up more often, and the push chances on those numbers are fitted from past games. Underdog rule: bet the model's pick only when it is priced 2.00 to 2.60. It is the best backtested spot so far but unproven going forward.

cfb.injuries: no injury data for college (use overrides/adjustments.csv for big news)
cfb.injury_text: College teams publish no reliable injury reports, so the model assumes everyone plays. Put big news (a starting QB out is often worth 3 to 7 points) in overrides/adjustments.csv.
cfb.early_text: Ratings still lean on last season, recruiting talent and returning production for the first few weeks. In the backtest, weeks 1 to 2 were where the model trailed the market most.
cfb.subtitle: Win chances and minimum prices from opponent-adjusted scoring and per-play efficiency, recruiting talent, returning production, home field, rest and travel, blended with the current spread where there is one. Total points are the stats model alone.
cfb.foot_note: Win % and margin blend the stats model with the current spread (ESPN's listed line): about 32% stats in the mix, fitted on 2023+ games. Out of sample (2024 on) the blend's log loss was 0.451 against the market's 0.452; the stats model alone was 0.464. Games with no price yet show the stats model alone. FBS games only (FCS opponents included). Margins bunch on 3 and 7, and the line calculator uses a smooth curve, so lines on those numbers are slightly off. Market comparisons use ESPN's listed lines from 2023 on.
